correctness.rationale: The seven types exhaust all choices by permutation of the q−1 right nongateways. The inverse grounded diagonal is resistance to the shorted leaders. The single-ground K_q inverse is (I+11ᵀ)/q; two grounds give (I+11ᵀ/2)/q on the followers. Write C for the single-ground right clique matrix and β=t/(1+t). For NG the left contribution is 1/(1+t) and the right trace is 2(q−1)/q. For NN block elimination of a gives C+βe_be_bᵀ; its rank-one inverse and the reinstated a diagonal give NG−NN=β(q+2−2qβ)/[q(q+2β)], the submitted factorization. GG and GN follow from the single-ground inverse, adding a conductance-t shunt at b in GN. With both leaders in one clique the other is connected to ground only through the bridge; series resistance and the one/two-ground diagonals recover AA, BV and VV, also for q=3. The five submitted strict gap certificates and the six exact differences were checked symbolically, with a separate direct full-matrix rational check at q=3,4 and t=3/2. Thus only NN and NG can tie, and only at (q+2)/(q−2); multiplicities and the inverse-trace/variance factor of two are correct. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed; the finite comparisons are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The comparable indexed unequal-clique theorem states p≥3 and is not a formal theorem-level inclusion of p=2. Its available proof, however, gives exactly the costs and strict comparison for every surviving p=2 orbit by substituting p=2 and dropping the impossible two-internal-leader orbit on the small side, with the zero-size follower class already handled. This is derivational coverage of the Finding, not an inference of priority from dates. The older general leader-selection frameworks alone are not the reason for failure.
residual_risks: The indexed comparator's catalogue path date postdates the frozen path's date. Neither this nor the exact specialization establishes historical priority, direction of derivation, provenance or authorship.
